A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across reordering and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F report original GMM simulations and CyTOF experiments, including clustering accuracy, convergence, runtime, and baseline comparisons.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix G retain original experiments and add CIFAR-10, kernel clustering, cluster-number misspecification, imbalance, and runtime-scaling results.

M1.justification: The product-manifold formulation and cubic-regularized Newton procedure remain intact. Although v1 already discusses kernelization conceptually in Appendix A, v2 Appendix G explicitly implements kernel-matrix input; this variant cannot use the original factor-based linear-time subproblem solver.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual CIFAR-10 image-clustering evaluation, previously mentioned only through prior work, and RBF-kernel clustering on Circles and Moon datasets. It also adds GMM scenarios with incorrect supplied cluster counts and controlled unequal cluster proportions, substantially broadening coverage beyond the retained GMM and CyTOF experiments.

E2.justification: The corresponding original comparisons retain their comparator membership, including NLR, SC, NMF, KM++, Carson's method, RTR, and I-AManPG. Added scenarios reuse subsets of these methods. The newly cited hybrid SDP methods are discussed but not evaluated as new baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include CIFAR-10 ViT-B-16 features reduced from 768 to 50 dimensions and 1,000-image subsamples; NMI evaluation with supplied cluster counts 3 or 5 when the truth is 4; and RBF bandwidths 3 and 15. The imbalance experiment uses r = K + 3, and new runtime sweeps vary r and d at n = 1000. These are additions, not documented changes to retained experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds explicit tests of robustness to incorrect cluster counts and controlled GMM imbalance, kernel-clustering case studies, and runtime sensitivity to rank and feature dimension. Earlier initialization and convergence analyses remain. The claimed additional large-penalty rank analysis is not visibly supplied: Figure 6 retains its original two panels.

E5.justification: Retained experiments preserve their 50-initialization or 50-repetition reporting and distribution plots. CIFAR-10 also uses 50 trials, continuing the existing practice. No increased repetition count for retained experiments or new confidence-interval, significance-testing, or seed-reporting procedure is documented.

E6.justification: V2 adds CIFAR-10 error distributions, misspecified-cluster-count NMI and convergence results, kernel-clustering outcomes, imbalance results, and approximately cubic-in-r and linear-in-d runtime trends. Figure 3's runtime measurements change, with the stated per-step cost revised from approximately 30–100 to 25–100 NLR steps. The 152-versus-80k iteration comparison and most original plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the missing one-half coefficient in Equation (11), repairs the completing-square argument in the LICQ proof (v1 Lemma 4; v2 Lemma 3), and corrects derivative expressions in Appendix F, including a missing commutation factor. Appendix B adds an explicit tightness argument. These are localized mathematical additions and repairs; the central assumptions and theorem guarantees remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.1 retain the same principal contributions: the manifold reformulation, Newton subproblems linear in sample size, second-order convergence complexity, and faster empirical convergence with comparable statistical accuracy. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the headline contribution.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the earlier rank-insensitivity recommendation: larger rank may help when the penalty is large or clusters are imbalanced. It adds an explanation linking imbalance to harmonic-mean cluster sizes and separation requirements, interprets the new misspecification results, and explicitly limits the linear-time guarantee for kernel inputs. These materially expand the applicability boundaries and practical guidance.

D1.justification: V2 newly provides a repository link described as containing a Python demonstration and GMM/CyTOF scripts, while acknowledging incomplete experiment coverage. It adds feature-processing and kernel settings, joint penalty/rank tuning guidance, and revised derivative and pseudocode instructions. These substantially expand reproduction resources; hardware and license disclosures were already present in v1.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds a focused comparison with four hybrid low-rank SDP works, distinguishing their augmented-Lagrangian treatment from the proposed feasibility-preserving approach. V2 also adds the Cartis et al. cubic-regularization reference and the Vision Transformer reference. The broader positioning and existing cited works remain.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. V2 makes localized explanatory and terminology edits, moves the formulation appendix after the proofs, adds a tightness subsection, and introduces acknowledgments, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements. This is a limited reorganization rather than a comprehensive rewrite.

P2.justification: Five new figures provide substantial multi-panel displays for misspecification, CIFAR-10, kernel clustering, imbalance, and runtime scaling. All fourteen original figures remain, with relocation, resizing, renumbering, and some caption changes. Figure 3's runtime panel is updated. Figure 6 introduces a presentation defect: its revised caption describes three panels although only two are displayed.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens practical validation by testing incorrect cluster counts, controlled imbalance, image embeddings, and nonlinear clustering, while examining rank and dimension costs. It also repairs mathematical and implementation formulas and supplies code-access guidance. These address important gaps in applicability evidence and reproducibility in v1. The missing panel described by Figure 6 and incomplete code coverage limit the gains, but do not outweigh them; benign nonconvexity still remains an assumption.
